column2: the python helper must preserve the existing session-key ladder and empty-cwd default so no-session reads keep the same counter partitioning as the bash hook; otherwise unrelated invocations can collapse into one bucket or split incorrectly.
the on-disk state contract must keep the hashed basename and a tab-separated hashed-path row; otherwise the helper can leak raw file paths or drift from the shipped state layout.

the wrapper must forward hook json unchanged and short-circuit non-read invocations before any filesystem or hashing work; otherwise bash calls can consume stdin, do unnecessary state work, or silently disable reminders.
the reminder output must be exact: emit only the posttooluse json envelope at the third read, and keep `additionalcontext` fixed so it never echoes a requested path or basename.

python/larch/core/hook_anti_read_poll.py:77 prior fallback fix is incomplete: discriminator must be non-empty, not merely set. scenario: current bash uses `${hook_anti_read_poll_discriminator:-}` with `-n`; an exported empty discriminator still falls back to `nosession`. the plan says "is set", which can change that bucket to `nosession-` and regress shipped partitioning.
